items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-12-23
items.q: he thought that King Oliver would hire him and let me go

ctx.x: Happy left around, let me see, King of Chicago, some show, I don't know if it was back and back. I don't know what show it was, I mean, but he came to the show and he left the show because he thought that King Oliver would hire him and let me go, but it didn't happen like that. It didn't happen like that.
That was when you were with King of Chicago.

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1960-01-28
items.q: King would give them ideas, I mean, he'd tell the guys if he wanted, the sax, sax, and that's just some commercial tunes, I mean, well, he'd dress them up, I mean, he'd cut out some parts, you know.

ctx.x: Who arranged these tunes like this?

Oh, well, I tell you, it didn't have no arrangement, I mean, it's, King would give them ideas, you know what I mean? King would give them ideas, I mean, he'd tell the guys if he wanted, the sax, sax, and that's just some commercial tunes, I mean, well, he'd dress them up, I mean, he'd cut out some parts, you know.
Let's hold it a minute, I want to get some. Someday sweetheart, King Oliver again.

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-01-07
items.q: And a couple of times I went with King Oliver, with Joe Oliver, I mean, I worked at Pete Lada's place.

ctx.x: You know, I've been about 25. Huh? No, he wasn't that old. You weren't 25 years old. No. I didn't know much. I was a little. I had to put on long pants to go play. I had to put on long pants to go play. 16 or 15 years old when he started. I don't know if he was that. No. I had to put on long pants to go play. I had to put on long pants to go play. 16 or 15 years old when he started. I don't know if he was that. No. He was stabbed in heaven. He had to put on long pants. He had to put on long pants because he was…

And then when I used to go work in the red light district. I used to go over there, he'd come and get me a little little fellow, a little kind of trouble, a friend of my union. Come at the house and tell me his dad said to go to his place at Rice's. And I put on, I had a pair of old long pants and stripes and it was heavy, big summertime, heavy piece of goods. And I put those long trousers on and go up there and play. Play with Manion and them. Manion and Francis had to wake Rice. They'd wake there a long time,…
I loved it a kid. Whose band was at Fue Clothes?

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: And then I relief Henry Zeno at Pete Lala. I used to relief him there. When King Oliver had the band, Joe Oliver had the band.

ctx.x: They always do it the same way. They used to.

That's right. Right. That's right. You hit the first note on the right foot? Yeah, right on the right foot, yeah. What places did you play in the district? Oh, in the district? Let me see. I worked at, I didn't work regular. I mean I, I relief old man Contrell at Rice. I used to relief him there. And then I relief Henry Zeno at Pete Lala. I used to relief him there. When King Oliver had the band, Joe Oliver had the band. He wasn't King then. It was Joe, Joe Oliver. And then I played at Few Clothes a few times.…
